alt="Archiving a session from the session dropdown context menu" style="max-width:100%;"> Keep your active session list clean by archiving old conversations instead of deleting them. You can archive a session by right-clicking on the session dropdown (not expanding it) and then selecting Archive. This hides it from the session dropdown. You can toggle the visibility of archived sessions by clicking the eye icon on the toolbar to the left of the dropdown. There is also a toolbar button to archive the session, you can use either option. The session context menu also provides **Archive All** and **Archive Others**. Archive All hides every listed session; Archive Others hides every listed session except the currently selected one. If Archive All leaves no visible sessions, the mini assistant closes; Archive Others keeps the selected session available. Archiving is a BeanBot feature, not the Harness. For agents that publish a session list, BeanBot filters archived rows after fetching them from the server — the conversation is still on the server. For [[Gemini Agent]], sessions are tracked only on this machine: archive hides them in the dropdown; there is no remote list to keep them on. > [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > [[Message History]] > [[Renaming the session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Options Panel Reference</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Customise the plugin behavior by navigating to `Tools > Options > BeanBot`. Here, you can configure the path to the Harness, add process arguments, set a global system Preamble for all sessions, and toggle **Local Echo** for instant message rendering. You can also adjust UI preferences like toolbar icon size, chat font size, enable or disable specific features (like Stash Diff or Jump to file), and set a custom user avatar. Additionally, the plugin includes a background **Update Checker Service** that automatically queries for new releases (with randomised intervals between 16 and 24 hours). You can toggle the update checks under `Tools > Options > BeanBot > Check for updates`. When an update is found, you will be prompted with a dialog to download the update immediately, get reminded later, or skip the version entirely. This page describes every preference in the panel, organised into six sections. A one-character marker next to an option name tells you when its value takes effect, and a legend line at the top of the panel repeats the key. **¹** means the running IDE only reads that value while it starts, so the change applies after you restart NetBeans — a bar at the top of the panel lists what is still waiting, and your sessions are restored automatically after the restart. **³** means the change applies to sessions you create from then on; sessions already open keep the value they started with. **²** means the current chat keeps the old setting until its history is reloaded. Options without a marker take effect as soon as you click **Apply** or **OK**. ##### 1. Assistant Service <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Path to Agent Server Binary</strong></td><td>Empty</td><td>The full path to the harness executable. If left blank, nothing runs until you pick a harness through the [[Onboarding]] screen. Use <strong>Browse...</strong> to pick a binary. Invalid paths show a validation error (e.g. <em>File not found</em>, <em>File is not executable</em>).</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Process Arguments</strong></td><td><code>acp</code> (harness-specific)</td><td>Extra command-line arguments passed when launching the server process. The chooser fills this from the harness catalog — most agents use <code>acp</code>; [[Gemini Agent]] uses <code>--acp --model gemini-3.8-flash</code> and [[Copilot Agent]] uses <code>--acp</code>. Change <code>--model</code> here if you want a different Gemini model. When Gemini is selected, a reminder appears under this field.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Harness</strong></td><td>Auto-detect</td><td>The agent the configured executable launches. <strong>Auto-detect</strong> reads the binary's file name and names the detected agent inline. A container launcher cannot be detected, so when the path is <code>docker</code>, <code>podman</code>, <code>nerdctl</code> or <code>finch</code> the field asks you to choose the harness running inside the image — for example path <code>/usr/bin/docker</code>, arguments <code>run --rm -i &lt;image&gt; acp</code>, harness <em>Goose</em>. An explicit choice wins over detection and survives path changes; a conflicting binary name shows a one-click switch instead of replacing your choice. Marked <em>¹</em>.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Launch through WSL (Windows only)</strong></td><td>Off</td><td>When enabled, all Harness invocations (running the daemon and token-usage stats for supported agents) are wrapped through <strong>WSL</strong> using <code>wsl.exe</code>. The resolved Windows executable is automatically translated to its WSL mount path, so custom/WinGet/Choco-shim install locations resolve correctly. If the Harness is installed as a native Linux binary inside WSL (no Windows executable found), it is invoked directly on the WSL PATH.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Browse...</strong></td><td>—</td><td>Opens a file chooser to select the executable.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 2. Updates <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Check for Updates</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the background <strong>Update Checker Service</strong>, which queries for new releases at randomised intervals between 16 and 24 hours. When an update is found you can download it immediately, get reminded later, or skip that version. A check can also be run on demand from the toolbar's help menu (<strong>Check for Updates</strong>).</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 3. Chat Behavior <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Echo user input immediately (Local Echo)</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Renders your message instantly in the chat while the server is processing, instead of waiting for the first response.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Session Idle Timeout (seconds)</strong></td><td>600</td><td>How long (0–3600, step 5) a request may sit idle — with no data arriving from the server — before it is failed. This is an <em>idle</em> timeout, not an absolute deadline, so long-running responses that keep streaming are never cut off.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Combine tool and thought bubbles into a single accordion</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Groups tool outputs and reasoning into one expandable header instead of separate bubbles. Takes effect after the session is reloaded. Marked <em>²</em>.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Auto-backup uncommitted changes on turn start (git/hg) (Experimental)</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Stashes uncommitted changes in git/hg repositories before each turn, so the AI can be rolled back safely.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Max Displayed Messages</strong></td><td>100</td><td>The maximum number of visible bubbles (10–200, step 5) kept in the chat panel before older ones are trimmed from the view to conserve memory. The full history remains on the server and can be reloaded.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 4. Actions <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Enable Sort Lines editor context menu actions</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Sort Lines Ascending</strong> and <strong>Sort Lines Descending</strong> items to the editor's right-click context menu.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Minify JSON editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Minify JSON</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for stripping formatting whitespace from JSON.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Search Web editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Search Web</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for searching the selected text (or the word under the cursor) on Google.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Toggle Annotations editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Toggle Annotations</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for toggling the versioning system's blame annotations.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable View File History editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>View File History</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for opening the versioning system's history view, plus git/Mercurial versioning window enhancements: a Refresh button and a Copy Message item on commit rows in the Show History window, and a Locate in System item in the Show Changes context menu. Requires an IDE restart to apply.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Stash Diff toolbar button and action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the <strong>Stash Diff</strong> toolbar button and the <code>Ctrl + Shift + L</code> action for viewing git stash diffs.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Jump to file dialog</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the <strong>Jump to File</strong> dialog (a shortcut, e.g. <code>Ctrl + Alt + J</code>, is shown next to the label when one is available).</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Copy All in Action Items</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds a copy button to NetBeans' Action Items toolbar that copies every task in the active scope and filters — including tasks hidden inside collapsed groups — as a plain-text list, with file and location details when available.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Mini Assistant</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Decides where <strong>Send to Assistant</strong> / <strong>Ask Assistant</strong> actions open: the floating mini dialog (enabled) or the main sidebar (disabled).</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Task Repository</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the todo.txt task management feature. When disabled, no task repositories are loaded, the Tasks Dashboard is hidden, and AI task tools (e.g. <code>add&#95;task</code>) are unavailable.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable ACP server restart on project switch (Experimental)</strong></td><td>Off</td><td>Binds the ACP server's working directory to the project of the session being opened, restarting the server when that project changes. The setting wins for every harness, including goose. Off by default while the feature stabilises; the panel shows a note that a project switch restarts the server and ends every session it is serving. When disabled, the server keeps the directory it was started with and only a manual restart or an IDE restart rebinds it — except that goose moves the loaded session's working directory in place, so that session opens in its own project without a restart. Marked <em>¹</em>.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 5. Appearance <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Custom User Icon (PNG)</strong></td><td>(empty)</td><td>Path to a PNG used as your avatar in chat. Click <strong>Browse...</strong> to pick one, or right-click the preview to clear it. Changing it reloads the session.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Toolbar Icon Size</strong></td><td>24</td><td>Icon size for the assistant toolbar: 16, 24, 28, 32, or 48. Marked <em>¹</em>.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Chat Font Size</strong></td><td>Inherited</td><td>Font size for chat text: Inherited (uses the theme), or 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16. Existing chats keep their current size until the session is reloaded. Marked <em>²</em>.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 6. alt="Attachments" style="max-width:100%;"> You can attach files and images to provide more context to the AI. Click the **Paperclip icon** in the input area to open the attachment menu. The paperclip icon displays a numeric badge showing how many files are currently attached, so attachments are visible at a glance. The plugin also supports dragging and dropping files directly into the chat, as well as pasting screenshots straight from your clipboard (you need a vision-capable model). Text and code files (Markdown, JSON, Java, YAML, …) are sent with their full content. When the agent supports embedded context the file travels as an embedded resource, otherwise its content is inlined into the prompt as a text block; other binary files that cannot be embedded are sent as a file reference. Images are sent as image content blocks. > [[Swing Mockups via Matisse]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Chat Features]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Configuration Template</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> ##### opencode.json This is the starter configuration the plugin writes when you accept the global-config setup prompt. alt="Mini Assistant" style="max-width:100%;"> The **Mini Assistant** is a compact, floating chat dialog that gives you quick access to the AI without needing the full sidebar panel. It shares the same session as the main assistant, so conversations stay in sync. You can disable it entirely under `Options > BeanBot > Actions > Enable Mini Assistant` — when disabled, "Send to Assistant" / "Ask Assistant" actions open the main sidebar instead. The Mini-Assistant was developed with one very specific usecase in mind, the window stays on top, so you can position it at the top right of the screen, `Ctrl + Alt + L` will toggle focus to the active editor, another `Ctrl + Alt + L` will focus the Mini-Assistant again, so you can generate snippets of code or select specific lines of code and refactor or analyze it without needing the full sidebar. It shows only the last assistant response, to see previous messages use `Page Up` or `Page Down` keys. > [[Opening the Mini Assistant]] > [[Using the Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]] > [[Differences from the main panel]] > [[Ask Assistant Menu]] / [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Check token usage]] > [[Options Panel Reference]]<div style="display: flex; It summarises every harness from data captured locally in the IDE: session, message and active-day counts, plus total cost, per-day averages, per-session token averages and median, and the summed **Input**, **Output** and **Cache Read** figures. Pick a day window and filter to the current project or all projects, then press **Refresh**. Hover over the status label (which normally says "Ready") to view the context window fill level. This helps you decide when to run `/compact` to summarise the conversation and free up context. The **Internal MCP Calls** table counts every call the agent made to the plugin's own tools, one row per tool, with a bar for each tool's share of the window and a **3 failed** style note when some of its executions ended in an error. Calls made while no session is active are still counted. **Note:** These figures are approximate. They are assembled from the usage data each harness reports, and harnesses report it differently — some include the cached read in their input count, and subscription-backed or free models often report no cost at all, so **Total Cost** understates their usage. Expect minor discrepancies: treat the panel as a close estimate of your usage, not an exact bill, and do not be surprised if it differs slightly from your provider's own dashboard. > [[Resetting context limits (/compact)]] > [[Time to first token]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Commands</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Slash commands let you perform quick actions directly from the chat input. Type `/` in the input area to trigger the autocomplete popup. Local commands are handled entirely by the plugin (never sent to the server): * `/new` — start a new session (shows a project picker when multiple projects are open) * `/title My Title` — rename the current session directly; `/title` without arguments asks the AI to suggest and apply a title * `/archive` — toggle archiving (hiding) the current session * `/model` / `/models` — open the model selector * `/agents` — open the agent selector * `/level` — open the thinking-level selector * `/sessions` — open the session dropdown Server commands (e.g. `/compact`, `/dcp`) are forwarded to the harness but appear in the same popup. Note: the Mini Assistant hides the selectors (`/model`, `/models`, `/agents`, `/level`, `/sessions`); use the main panel or keyboard shortcuts for those. Each command links to a fuller explanation: > `/new` — [[Starting a Session]] > `/models`, `/agents`, `/level` — [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > `/sessions` — [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > `/archive` — [[Archiving Sessions]] > `/title` — [[Renaming the session]] > `/compact` — [[Resetting context limits (/compact)]] > Typing `/` — [[Slash Command Autocomplete]]<div alt="Slash command autocomplete popup listing the available commands" style="max-width:100%;"> Typing `/` in the input area opens an autocomplete popup listing all available commands — the plugin's local commands plus the server commands advertised by the harness. Keep typing to narrow the list. Use Up/Down to highlight an entry, then press `Enter` or `Tab` to insert the highlighted command into the input. If the typed text exactly matches a command name, pressing `Enter` sends it immediately. The popup disappears when you press `Escape`, type a space, or click away. See [[Commands]] for the full list of available commands and what each one does.<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Input Area Keys</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The chat input area supports these keyboard shortcuts: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Enter</code></td><td>Send the message</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Shift + Enter</code></td><td>Insert a newline</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Tab</code></td><td>Switch agent / open the options panel</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + Up</code> / <code>Alt + Down</code></td><td>Recall previous / next message from history</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + R</code></td><td>Open the History Search dialog (type to filter, Up/Down to navigate)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Z</code> / <code>Ctrl + Y</code></td><td>Undo / Redo</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Escape</code></td><td>Close popups and refocus the input</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Message History]] > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Slash Command Autocomplete]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Ask Assistant Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Two editor menu entries launch the Mini Assistant for refactoring help: * Right-click in the editor and choose **Refactoring > Ask Assistant...** to send the current selection to the assistant for refactoring. * Use the code generator — press `Alt + Insert` (or open the Insert Code menu) and pick **Ask Assistant** to generate code from a prompt. Both open (or focus) the Mini Assistant with your selected code attached as context. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Attachments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Inspector Context Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> After running inspections (e.g. via `Analyze > Inspect & Transform`), right-click any item in the **Inspector** window to see two actions: * **Copy** — copies the selected subtree (filename, line number and description of each problem) to the clipboard as text. * **💬 Send to Assistant** — pre-fills the Mini Assistant input with the same text, so you can edit it before sending. The same **Copy** / **💬 Send to Assistant** actions are also available in the **Test Results** window on failed tests. > [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Send to Assistant</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The **💬 Send to Assistant** context action sends code or file context straight into the assistant for you to refine before sending: * **Editor:** Right-click selected code in the editor and choose **Send to Assistant** to open the assistant with the selection pre-filled. * **Projects / Explorer:** Right-click a file node and choose **Send to Assistant** to send that file's path as context. * **Inspector / Test Results:** Right-click an inspection problem or a failed test to send its details for diagnosis. Repeated sends **append** to the input instead of replacing it, so you can gather several snippets before sending. Which assistant opens (the floating Mini Assistant or the main sidebar) is controlled by the **Enable Mini Assistant** checkbox under `Options > BeanBot > Actions`. When context-menu additions are disabled, these actions are hidden from the menus. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Ask Assistant Menu]] > [[Inspector Context Menu]] / [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Options Panel Reference]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Test Results Context Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> After running a test suite, right-click any failed test (or failure tree) in the **Test Results** window to access two actions: * **Copy** — copies the selected failure subtree (test name, file, line and failure message) to the clipboard as text. * **💬 Send to Assistant** — pre-fills the Mini Assistant input with the same text so you can ask for a diagnosis or fix. These actions share the same popup helper (`TreePopupSupport`) as the Inspector window. > [[Inspector Context Menu]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; alt="Jump to File dialog for searching files across open projects" style="max-width:100%;"> The **Jump to File** dialog (`Ctrl + Alt + J`, or `Cmd + Option + J` on Mac) lets you open any file across all open projects by typing part of its name. It matches case-insensitively by filename prefix, path substring, or glob patterns. Navigate with the arrow keys and press `Enter` to open. The dialog is backed by an in-memory index that rebuilds in the background and updates live as files change. It first looks for a project-root `.bbignore` — same syntax as `.gitignore`, but tuned for what you want to see rather than what version control tracks — and when one exists it uses only that file, skipping `.gitignore`/`.hgignore`. Without a `.bbignore` it falls back to the project's VCS ignore file. Enable or disable it under `Options > BeanBot`. > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[IDE Enhancements]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: alt="Message pinning" style="max-width:100%;"> Assistant messages can be pinned so they stay visible even as older messages are hidden from the chat to conserve memory. Hover over an assistant bubble and click the pin icon to pin (or unpin) it. Pins are stored per session and persist across restarts, making it easy to keep a plan or to-do list on screen while the rest of the conversation scrolls away. > [[Message History]] > [[Filtering Chat Messages]] > [[Copying a message]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Session Dropdown Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Right-click a session in the session dropdown to get a quick action menu: * **Rename** — give the session a custom name * **Archive / Unarchive** — hide or show the session * **Archive All** — hide every session in the dropdown * **Archive Others** — hide every session except the selected one * **Reload** — re-fetch the session from the server This mirrors the toolbar buttons for rename, archive, and reload. Archive All and Archive Others are available from the context menu when there are sessions to archive. > [[Renaming the session]] > [[Archiving Sessions]] > [[Message History]]<div style="display: alt="New Session Confirm Bar" style="max-width:100%;"> When you start a new session, a slide-in confirmation bar appears above the input area. On harnesses that can pick a model in-session it reads *"Select the agent, model and level below, then click Continue."* On [[Gemini Agent]], which has no in-session model dropdown, it reads *"Select the agent and level below, then click Continue."* The dropdowns stay locked until you confirm, so the session starts with the configuration you intend. Clicking **Continue** unlocks them and starts the session. > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Gemini Agent]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Auto-Backup on Turn Start</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Before each turn, the plugin can back up your uncommitted changes by stashing a copy (`git stash`, or `hg shelve`) so work can be retrieved safely if the AI makes unwanted modifications. The backup appears as an **Auto-Backup** tool bubble in the chat. This is enabled by default under `Options > BeanBot > Chat Behavior > Auto-backup uncommitted changes on turn start (git/hg)` and can be disabled there. If you see too many stashes piling up, you can ask the plugin to cleanup by sending a message like "Drop all stashes starting with the name beanbot except for the most recent 5" > [[Options Panel alt="The harness chooser listing installed and supported harnesses" style="max-width:100%;"> The plugin works with several coding harnesses that speak the Agent Client Protocol: **Oh My Pi**, **OpenCode**, **Codex**, **OpenClaw**, **Pi**, **Goose**, **Cursor**, **Copilot**, **Claude**, **Hermes**, **Gemini**, **Devin**, **Kilo Code**, **Cline**, and **Jcode**. When no harness binary is configured, the chat panel shows the **Coding Harness Configuration** screen instead of the normal input — it groups every supported harness by status so you can see at a glance what is ready to use. * The **Active Harness** card at the top shows the currently configured harness with its binary path and a disabled **Active** badge, and spells out how to sign in to that harness if it still needs authentication. The active harness is not repeated in the lists below. * **Installed Harnesses** lists every detected full-support harness with a **Use** button — clicking **Use** saves that harness (and its launch arguments) and asks you to restart NetBeans. The switch takes effect on the next start, so the running assistant is left alone; this also gives you time to sign in first. Every row also states how to authenticate the harness's CLI, with the command on a click-to-copy chip where one exists (for example <code>kilo auth login</code>, <code>agent login</code>, <code>goose configure</code> or <code>cline auth</code>); harnesses that sign in interactively on first run describe that flow instead. Each row has a disclosure triangle (`>`) that reveals the detected binary path. Gemini's default arguments include <code>--model gemini-3.8-flash</code>; change <code>--model</code> under Process Arguments in Options if you want a different model. * **Available for Installation** groups the full-support harnesses not found on your system, each with a **Get** button — clicking it reveals the OS-specific install command for that harness. Click the command to copy it to the clipboard and install the harness in a terminal. Each install panel also shows the sign-in command, any prerequisites the harness needs (for example, Node.js for the Claude adapter), a **Documentation** button, and a reminder to restart NetBeans afterwards so it can find the new binary on your `PATH`. * **Limited support** holds the harnesses whose ACP integration is only partial — currently **OpenClaw**, **Jcode**, **Gemini**, **Pi** and **Cline** — whether or not they are installed. The section is expanded by default and each row carries a muted **Limited** pill; hover it to see what that harness cannot do. Rows still offer **Use** or **Get** like any other, and clicking the section header collapses it when you want a shorter list. * A collapsible **Note** at the bottom sets the order: sign in to the harness's CLI once, then click **Use** and restart NetBeans when prompted. The assistant server starts with the IDE, so the new harness is what runs after the restart — and a fresh install also needs that restart before NetBeans can see the new `PATH`. * The **Manual Configuration** button (gear icon) opens the Assistant settings where you can browse for any binary path yourself — useful if your harness lives outside your `PATH`. Binaries found on `PATH` are never used automatically — you always make the choice through this screen. If a configured binary later disappears (for example after an uninstall), the chooser appears again. To re-run harness selection at any time — for example after installing a new harness or switching providers — click the **?** (help) button in the toolbar and choose **Run Harness Selection Again** from the popup menu. This reopens the same chooser with fresh detection results. After installing a harness — and optionally setting the binary path under `Options > BeanBot` — click **Start Server** to connect. > [[OpenCode]] / [[Codex Agent]] / [[PI Agent]] / [[Goose Agent]] / [[Cursor Agent]] / [[Copilot Agent]] > [[Claude Agent]] / [[Hermes Agent]] / [[Gemini Agent]] / [[Oh My Pi Agent]] / [[OpenClaw Agent]] / [[Devin Agent]] / [[Kilo Code Agent]] / [[Cline Agent]] / [[Jcode Agent]] > [[Post Install]] > [[Restarting the server]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Global Configuration Setup]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Update Notifications</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The plugin checks for new releases in the background at randomised 16–24 hour intervals. When an update is available, a dialog offers three choices: * **Download Now** — open the release to download and install * **Remind me Later** * **Skip this Version** Disable the check under `Options > BeanBot > Updates > Check for Updates`. You can also check on demand: click the **?** (help) button in the toolbar and choose **Check for Updates**. The outcome is shown on the status line (for example *You are up to date* or *An update is available*). > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Post Install]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Customising the Toolbar</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Right-click anywhere on the assistant toolbar to open the **Edit ToolBar** popup, which lists every toolbar button with a checkbox. Uncheck buttons you don't use (e.g. export, restart, mini assistant) and they disappear; check them again to restore. Your choices are saved and persist across IDE restarts. The toolbar provides quick access to actions like starting a session, checking token usage, restarting the server, and exporting conversations. The **?** (help) button opens a popup menu with four items: **Open User Guide** (opens this guide in your browser), **Check for Updates** (queries for a new release immediately), **Show Keyboard Shortcuts** (shows the shortcuts dialog), and **Run Harness Selection Again** (lets you switch between installed coding harnesses). The icon size is set separately under `Options > BeanBot > Appearance > Toolbar Icon Size`. > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Markdown Project Type</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> **Markdown Project** is a minimal project type for folders of plain text, notes, or documentation — no compiler or build system needed. To create one, choose `Tools > New Project > Other > Markdown Project`, or just run `touch .mdproject` inside any folder to make it loadable as a project. It renders a clean directory tree in the Projects tab, filters OS junk and editor swap files, and can be closed or deleted from the project node's right-click menu. It's a handy workspace for chatting about a folder of text files — and for managing configuration. > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[IDE Enhancements]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If you have strict privacy requirements or want to avoid API costs, you can run the plugin entirely offline using local LLMs: 1. Install a local runner like [Ollama](https://ollama.com) and download a coding model (e.g., `ollama run deepseek-coder` or `ollama run qwen2.5-coder`). 2. Add a configuration block for the local model in your `opencode.json` configuration file. Note that Qwen models might require `--think=false` if configured via Ollama, and a `"reasoningEffort": "none"` entry. 3. Open the chat options panel (click the gear icon or press `Tab` in the input area) and choose your local model from the dropdown list. All code queries and indexing tasks will now execute locally on your machine. Other harnesses have similar support either via their CLI or TUI interfaces. > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Install Ollama]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Copying a message</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can copy individual user messages back into the input text-area. Hover over the user icon, it'll change into a copy button — clicking it copies the message to the clipboard and adds it to the input text-area so you can resend or edit it. Assistant responses can be copied by hovering over the bubble, you'll see a copy and a pin button, copy will copy to the clipboard. > [[Pinned Messages]] > [[Message History]] > [[Starting a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Experiments</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Here are some interesting things you can try with the plugin: > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Local Data Analysis in Java]] > [[Swing Mockups via Matisse]] > [[Markdown Project Type]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Exporting a conversation</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <img alt="Export Conversation" style="max-width:100%;"> The share button on the toolbar exports the session to a file. Clicking it opens a small menu where you can choose between **Markdown** and **HTML** — HTML output mimics the sidebar chat view, including the expandable activity panels and chat styling. > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > [[Message History]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Filtering Chat Messages</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> To reduce clutter in your chat history, you can selectively show or hide different message types using the **Filter** button on the toolbar. Clicking this button opens a dropdown menu allowing you to toggle the visibility of: * **Activity**: Hides or shows tool outputs and internal model reasoning chains together. * **Assistant**: Hides or shows the assistant's responses. * **User**: Hides or shows your own messages. If the option to combine tools and thoughts is disabled in your settings, the menu will dynamically update to show individual checkboxes for **Tool** outputs and **Thought** reasoning. Your filter choices are instantly applied to the active chat thread and are automatically saved so they persist across NetBeans IDE restarts. > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Chat Features]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Instead of creating temporary branches for minor changes or code drafts, you can save your progress as stashes and use the Stash Diff viewer as a visual sandbox: 1. Save your experimental code in a stash: `git stash`. 2. Open the NetBeans Git Repository Browser, select the stash, and press `Ctrl + Shift + L` (or click **Diff Stash** in the toolbar). 3. Simulate a merge by comparing it against **To HEAD**, or see how it fits with other local changes by comparing it against **To Working Tree**. 4. If you only want specific changes, right-click files in the diff list and choose **"Apply this change"** to cherry-pick them back into your working tree without applying the entire stash. > [[IDE Enhancements]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Auto-Backup on Turn Start]] > [[MCP Tools]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">IDE Enhancements</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The plugin integrates deeply with NetBeans beyond just the chat panel to boost your coding productivity: <div style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">Markdown Project Type</div> * Allows you to create a minimal project for managing folders of text notes, design files, or markdown documentation without requiring a compiler or build system (e.g., Maven or Gradle). * To create one, go to `Tools > New Project > Other > Markdown Project`. Alternatively, you can run `touch .mdproject` inside any folder to instantly make that directory loadable as a project in NetBeans. * It is identified by a `.mdproject` marker file, and renders a clean directory tree in the NetBeans Projects tab, automatically filtering out OS junk files and editor swap files. * You can close or delete the project directly from the right-click context menu on the project node. <div style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">Stash Diff</div> * A side-by-side diff viewer for git stashes. Select any stash in the NetBeans Git Repository Browser and press `Ctrl + Shift + L` (or click the **Diff Stash** button in the Git toolbar) to open it. * **To Base (default):** Displays stash parent commit vs stash content (equivalent to `git stash show -p`). * **To HEAD:** Simulates a 3-way merge applying the stash on your current HEAD, showing conflict markers inline (with a red "Conflict" label in the right panel if conflicts occur). * **To Working Tree:** Simulates applying the stash onto the working tree, showing unchanged/modified tree status on the left. * **File List & Partial Apply:** Click any file to view its syntax-highlighted diff, or right-click a file to "Apply this change" individually from the stash. <div style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">Editor Context Menu Utilities</div> * **Search Web:** Right-click selected text (or the word under the cursor) in the editor and click **Search Web** to quickly search Google using your NetBeans-configured web browser. * **Sort Lines Ascending / Descending:** Select multiple lines, right-click, and choose this option to alphabetically sort them. * **Minify JSON:** Right-click any JSON content to quickly strip out all formatting whitespace. * **Toggle Annotations:** Right-click in the editor and choose **Toggle Annotations** to toggle the versioning system's blame annotations for the file. * **View File History:** Right-click in the editor and choose **View File History** to open the versioning system's history view for the file. For git and Mercurial, the Show History window gains a **Refresh** button that re-runs the search and **Copy Message** on commit rows, and the Show Changes window gains **Locate in System** to open the selected file's folder in your file manager. * Each of these context menu items can be enabled or disabled independently under `Tools > Options > BeanBot`. <div style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">Action Items Copy</div> * Adds a copy button to NetBeans' Action Items toolbar that copies every task in the current scope and filters — including tasks hidden inside collapsed groups — as a plain-text list, with file and location details when available. * Can be enabled or disabled under `Tools > Options > BeanBot` (**Enable Copy All in Action Items**). <div style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">Jump to File</div> * A modeless file search dialog triggered via `Ctrl + Alt + J` (or `Cmd + Option + J` on Mac) that lets you search all open projects by filename prefix, path substring, or glob patterns. * Supports quick keyboard navigation with arrow keys and `Enter` to open. * Powered by an **In-Memory File Indexing Cache** that rebuilds in the background when projects are opened or closed. It first honors a project-root `.bbignore` (same syntax as `.gitignore`, tuned for display); when present it replaces `.gitignore`/`.hgignore` entirely, otherwise the VCS ignore file applies. Common directories like `node_modules/`, `target/`, and `build/` are skipped when no VCS ignore strategy is available. * Includes incremental live indexing via file system listeners, meaning new, deleted, or renamed files are immediately searchable without full rebuilds. * Can be enabled or disabled under `Tools > Options > BeanBot`. > [[Markdown Project Type]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Jump to File]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Inspector Context Menu]] / [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] ---<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Keyboard Shortcuts</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Navigate and control the assistant efficiently using keyboard shortcuts: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + L</code></td><td>Toggle the assistant panel (open or close)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + Up</code> / <code>Alt + Down</code></td><td>Cycle through previously sent messages</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Page Up</code> / <code>Page Down</code></td><td>Scroll the chat</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + R</code></td><td>Search message history</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Alt + J</code> (or <code>Cmd + Option + J</code> on Mac)</td><td>Open the Jump to File dialog</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Shift + L</code></td><td>Open the Stash Diff viewer</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Alt + A</code> (or <code>Cmd + Option + A</code> on Mac)</td><td>Answer a pending permission request with Allow Once</td></tr> <tr><td><code>/</code></td><td>Open the slash command autocomplete popup</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Tab</code></td><td>Accept the highlighted autocomplete command and insert it into the input area</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Escape</code></td><td>Close options panel and refocus input</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Message History]] > [[Jump to File]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts Dialog]] > [[Expand/Collapse All]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Local Data Analysis in Java</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can use the assistant to run quick data processing tasks on local files (like `.csv` or log files) using single-file Java programs and have the results rendered directly in the chat: 1. **Prepare your Data**: Open a project or create a folder with some tabular data (e.g., `sales.csv`). 2. **Ask the Assistant to Analyse**: Ask the assistant to write a single-file Java program to analyze this data. * *Prompt:* `"Write a single-file Java program to read sales.csv, calculate the total revenue grouped by category, and print the results as an ASCII table."` 3. **Execute the Code**: Click **Accept** on the permission prompt to let the assistant write the file (e.g., `SalesAnalyzer.java`) and run it using the Java launcher (e.g., `java SalesAnalyzer.java`). 4. **View Formatted Output**: Since Java 11+, single-file source code can be run directly using the `java` launcher without manual compilation. Because the plugin renders ASCII tables as formatted HTML tables with alternating row colors, the printed output will display beautifully inside your chat bubble. > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Since the plugin supports the **Markdown Project** type (which lets you load any folder that has a `.mdproject` file in it), you can use it to manage your OpenCode configuration directly inside the IDE: 1. Navigate to your OpenCode configuration directory in your terminal: * **Linux/macOS:** `~/.config/opencode` * **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode` 2. Create an empty project marker file by running: * `touch .mdproject` (Linux/macOS) * `type nul > .mdproject` (Windows CMD) or `New-Item .mdproject` (PowerShell) 3. Open NetBeans and go to `File > Open Project`. Navigate to that configuration directory and open it. 4. You can now manage your configuration directly inside the IDE. Since the files are loaded as a project in NetBeans, you can ask the assistant panel to make changes for you (e.g., "Add a new custom agent config to my opencode.json") instead of editing them manually. > [[Markdown Project Type]] > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; alt="Message history search" style="max-width:100%;"> Your complete message history is always safely stored on the server. While the local chat view hides older messages to conserve IDE memory, you can always retrieve the full history by clicking **Show All Messages** followed by **Reload** — the session is reloaded but all messages are retained. You can also search through your past input history using `Ctrl + R`. If you want to keep just one or two messages visible (e.g. a plan or to-do list), hover over the response bubble and click the pin icon; pinned messages stay in the chat panel instead of being cleared over time. > [[Pinned Messages]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Exporting a conversation]] > [[Reloading a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Swing Mockups via Matisse</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can use the assistant to convert visual UI mockups (screenshots or wireframes) into Java Swing code, and enhance your Matisse GUI forms with custom components: 1. **Draft a Visual Mockup**: Draw a UI sketch or take a screenshot of a component you want to build. 2. **Generate the Custom Component**: Drag-and-drop the mockup image into the chat (or use the paperclip icon) and ask the assistant to code it. * *Prompt:* `"Analyze this mockup. Write a custom JComponent called GradientHeaderPanel.java that renders a color gradient background, a title label, and a drop shadow that matches this design."` 3. **Compile & Palette Import**: Let the assistant write the file, compile your project, and then drag the compiled `GradientHeaderPanel` class directly into the NetBeans **Matisse Palette**. 4. **Design visually with Matisse**: Open any Swing GUI form (like a `JFrame` or `JPanel`) in Matisse, and drag-and-drop your new custom AI-generated component directly from the Palette onto your form design. 5. **Hook up the Logic**: In your Matisse form, click the "Source" tab. Share the Matisse-generated class with the assistant and ask it to write the event listeners and backend logic for your visual components: * *Prompt:* `"Help me write the ActionListeners to connect the search button (btnSearch) to fetch results and populate the list model for lstResults."` > [[Attachments]] > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: alt="Permission Requests" style="max-width:100%;"> When the AI attempts to execute a tool, modify files, or run shell commands, the plugin ensures you remain in control. An Accept/Deny bubble will appear in the chat with full context of the requested action. You must explicitly grant permission before the operation proceeds. The permission configuration varies by harness, look at their respective documentation for details. The buttons follow whatever options the harness sends, so the exact set and wording vary: a harness may offer *Allow Once* and *Always Allow* side by side, a single *Allow*, or — as Claude does — word the same choices **Yes** / **No**. When the request includes file changes, a **Show Diff** button appears next to them so you can review the edit before approving. Each button has a keyboard mnemonic, so this panel never needs the mouse: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Alt + A</code></td><td>Always Allow</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + O</code></td><td>Allow Once — separate from <code>Alt + A</code>, so the two allow options are never ambiguous</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + R</code></td><td>Reject / Deny</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + W</code></td><td>Always Reject / Deny Always — the counterpart of <code>Alt + A</code> when a harness offers both reject options</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + D</code></td><td>Show Diff (opens the changes without answering the request)</td></tr> </tbody> </table> On macOS the same keys are <code>Option + A</code>, <code>Option + O</code>, <code>Option + R</code>, <code>Option + W</code> and <code>Option + D</code>. Swing normally binds a button's mnemonic to <code>Ctrl + Option</code> on a Mac (because <code>Option</code> types accented characters there), so the plugin binds the plain <code>Option</code> form itself as well; either combination answers the prompt. While a request is pending, <code>Ctrl + Alt + A</code> (<code>Cmd + Option + A</code> on Mac) answers it from anywhere in the IDE, always with Allow Once rather than a lasting policy. The letter belongs to the option's scope, not to its label: the harness reports a *once* or *always* kind (and, when it reuses one kind, an id that names the scope), and the plugin maps that to `Alt + O` / `Alt + R` for once and `Alt + A` / `Alt + W` for always, so no two buttons in a row ever share a key. Some harnesses word the buttons so the letter never appears — Claude sends **Yes** and **No** — but `Alt + O`, `Alt + A` and `Alt + R` still answer them; only the underline is missing. The same keys work in the mini assistant, see [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]]. The header button to the left of the mini-assistant latches break mode, shown as a padlock or a coffee cup. See [[Break Mode]]. > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> alt="Options panel with the agent, model and thinking level selectors" style="max-width:100%;"> Hitting `Tab` when in the input text-area or pressing the small gear icon, will slide open the chat options panel, by default you'll see pre-configured agents for that harness, most of the harnesses also allow custom agents to be defined, pick one of the models supported by the providers you have configured, and a suitable Thinking Level, the actual levels displayed depend on the exact model selected. The gear would have turned into a down arrow button, click the button to close the options panel. You can also use the `/agents`, `/models`, and `/level` slash commands to open these selectors. [[Gemini Agent]] does not offer an in-session model dropdown — set <code>--model</code> in Process Arguments instead (see [[Options Panel Reference]]). The [[New Session Confirm Bar]] prompt omits "model" for Gemini for the same reason. > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[New Session Confirm Bar]] > alt="Assistant Options" style="max-width:100%;"> The plugin adds a tab to the NetBeans Options — open the Options Window and you'll see an additional BeanBot tab at the end. In most cases, you can go with the defaults, but if the [[Onboarding]] screen couldn't auto-detect your harness, you can specify the full path to its binary there. The preamble is an additional user prompt that's sent to the server when creating a new chat session. The default text contains some directives around code quality, planning and task management, you can customise this with your own instructions. When you upgrade the NetBeans IDE to a new major version, the plugin automatically migrates your saved preferences and cached session data from the previous NetBeans user directory, so you do not need to reconfigure the assistant after an upgrade. > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Update Notifications]] > [[Onboarding]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Renaming the session</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> To keep your conversations organised, you can rename any session. Click the **Pencil icon** in the chat UI or right-click a session in the session dropdown to give it a custom name. Alternatively, type the `/title` slash command to let the AI automatically generate and apply a suitable title based on the conversation context. These custom names are stored locally by the plugin, not in the harness DB. > [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > [[Commands]] > [[Archiving Sessions]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Resetting context limits (/compact)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If your conversation becomes very long and you notice the AI starting to forget earlier details or slow down as it approaches its context token limits, you can reset the conversation context. Type the `/compact` command in the chat input. The assistant will summarise the history, code changes, and context discussed so far, replacing the verbose message history with a highly condensed summary. This resets the active token budget while preserving the essential goals and context of the thread. > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Check token usage]] > [[Reloading a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Restarting the server</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If the assistant becomes unresponsive or you experience connection issues, you can restart the underlying OpenCode background server. Click the **Restart Harness** button in the toolbar. This will safely terminate the current background process and spin up a new one, reconnecting your IDE without losing your saved sessions. > [[Onboarding]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > [[Auto-Reconnect]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Starting a Session</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <img src="data:image/webp;base64,UklGRsgDAABXRUJQVlA4TLsDAAAvmQAPAGcFKbJtV9Xa9zJjiG3sIAcNOcM5ix81wI1kW3V0zgMxejIVhfL3lAiZjLv3vXEdSbaqzD4cMuCTIImDMN1d7pn5F5om2Ey743i/Bigg0UMAgFCwiR7dZQPjjzjimO4j6fp+EolE7/gTiUTVGlG1Znc5Ef3b4/chqta84+/1/yMSdS/Pvy/RD+rx+xCJUkocr295/f+IqjXX95OoexG9409UrfmRdi8//5fxXNYwBBUCiB6vv9PfnhJAqXsBPA8zSoAKIdW/OkqH1puFORqJYrmdI3VG7sl6BUlJpIQEUEDCGAVISYAYBRgkxYERCWmOIilipKDOEw0UREqr3cscACNGMkYGCVhxzAoMjUg4RlJyYCzG2syWcETASIpZYtZOUmz3OwqvbwMwSLu2vZCkzI61tm3bHLOUse3usW1b6x3rV85Uqt5Ude+3OedNRP8duW0jSTTSWy0zp6ruL5B96Ln0HwvuC837zBxQst5DOUpFhWV+Nc9CeZ648jYkLjbk9eVjnjoPodL/LcGSYb+p2saacZjzz+NkVaMoVDn26bldjzWonKUVWLJt93e4UYixSYib0RpFVUZEQVGLvLpbqls54CH6d4nRaXO3VYrSl/unieeZByEKReWDTN3LxDzxG6xpFDUD5tcqVUIuECbXwzWqontZrB35Q7z7ahq6vE1HRFPlUzAxyKEIjVphdQ0RhWuYqGkU9d/J4cGWANMfeq7REMPCxwq1xHZuHuKOS1iobhRCDP0k/j7EzPF4Kl0wLo1aJC8f0SXMNDL5TcxzRaZfzMqVOEuFg7uq9Gq7ggDeqOKekSeSpg+1k4ONs7xUoNPBBtbKXrd7EYBvmnzSwKnHD/V5JLisbyBu7tnaQFwHKAUHNFs1c90aSCBiqUxg4ZJWUoxF+YhYVIwlYtlGizX6qu/1Ia5iLSHfIElrgEMFG0d5qShzGPwNyB7NVJs/QYTeWE4sJxbqFSTZ2WWukmnt1RewiylPfmItuUBXKWs2TjRX36jXyrRCJzJNmBR3g3fYWgLTap8p9rrdaDbuFR4RL0s0+ijXREzjXqt9fjAjGjq9CJznC41+CzZ2MIRqzzz53yTWUnHNTk36qjPdoyFvEh+DDeuzQiPPcj1mL1HYiakeX+TLLZO3r4shClWvESsIYb+GFt5CvKNSlL7eP03w9N1vEkXtGnEPtZ3mrfxv+VG3CIcMqAzrdSBit8FsfANeGnwZxbw6y/c1mZENStY7rq9J2+N54urbkLj40Nc3Thwh+6uCAA==" alt="Assistant toolbar and input area for starting a session" style="max-width:100%;"> Click the '+' button on the toolbar to start a new session, this will initialise the chat interface and post the preamble to the Harness (Tools > Options > BeanBot > Preamble). The input text-area is at the bottom of the sidebar panel, you'll see placeholder text that says *Type Message Here*, type your messages and press `Enter` to send to the server, the response will be rendered as a chat bubble, if you need to send multi-line text, press `Shift + Enter` to add a newline to the text-area. You can also type `/new` in the input area to quickly start a new session. Once the session is up, some agents (like the [[PI Agent]]) post a startup banner with their version, context files and extensions — the plugin renders it as a compact info card instead of a raw text bubble. > [[New Session Confirm Bar]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Welcome Screen]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Thinking and Tool Responses</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Advanced models use a "thinking" budget to reason before responding. This internal reasoning is displayed in its own collapsible pane. Similarly, when the AI uses tools, the tool output is shown in collapsible panes marked with a tag icon. You can use the **Filter** button to hide these thought or tool bubbles from the chat view, or use the **Expand/Collapse All** button to manage them all at once. By default, consecutive tool and thought bubbles are combined into a single expandable accordion, so you can collapse them together. You can turn this off under `Options > BeanBot > Combine tool and thought bubbles into a single accordion`. Error messages will appear as red-tinted bubbles, and tables are rendered cleanly with alternating row colours. > [[Filtering Chat Messages]] > [[Time to first token]] > [[Auto-Backup on Turn Start]] flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Home</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <i style="opacity: 0.7;">Last updated for BeanBot v1.30.0</i> BeanBot is a NetBeans plugin that provides an AI assistant panel that lets you chat with AI models directly inside the IDE to generate, refactor and understand code, it automatically attaches active project and source file context to your messages. It also features a built-in permission handler — allowing you to inspect code diffs before applying changes and explicitly approve file deletions or terminal commands. Originally based on OpenCode, it now also supports Pi, Goose, Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Gemini, Oh My Pi, Devin, Copilot, Codex, OpenClaw, Kilo Code, Cline and Jcode. <img
