alt="Break button pressed: the coffee cup" style="max-width:100%;"> </div> The header button to the left of the mini-assistant icon latches two states. Released, it shows a padlock and permission requests behave as described above. Pressed, it shows a coffee cup: you are on a break, and the plugin answers every permission request with **Allow Once** on its own — no prompt, no diff preview, nothing moves focus — until you press the button again. Arming it asks for confirmation once, because from that point on tool calls proceed without review. Releasing it never asks. Arming also gives the coffee icon one short two-beat pulse (about a second) so the change of state is caught even in peripheral vision; after that the icon stays still. The latched button, its tooltip and the auto-allowed result lines in the chat carry the state — there is no repeating blink. The mode lasts only for the current IDE session; it is never stored, so a restart returns to normal prompting. > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Jcode Agent</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> #### Install - **macOS / Linux / WSL**: `curl -fsSL https://jcode.sh/install | bash` - **Windows (PowerShell)**: `irm https://jcode.sh/install.ps1 | iex` The installer puts the <code>jcode</code> launcher in <code>~/.local/bin</code> (<code>%LOCALAPPDATA%\jcode\bin</code> on Windows) and keeps its versioned builds under <code>~/.jcode</code>. Docs: <a href="https://jcode.sh/docs" target="_blank" rel="noopener">jcode.sh/docs</a>. #### About <a href="https://jcode.sh/docs" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Jcode</a> is a coding agent with its own TUI and a background daemon. Running <code>jcode acp</code> makes it act as an **ACP server** over stdio: it speaks JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout and is meant to be spawned by an ACP-aware editor, so it is not a command to run yourself. The executable you configure in BeanBot is <code>jcode</code>, run with the default launch argument <code>acp</code>. **Authentication** is a CLI prerequisite: run <code>jcode login</code> once in a terminal (or import an existing provider credential — Jcode detects Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Pi credentials after asking) before connecting. Jcode advertises no ACP authenticate methods, so a fresh install without credentials fails <code>session/new</code> — sign in first, then pick Jcode in the chooser. Jcode in BeanBot supports: - [[Editor Context->Automatic Context Capture]] Seamlessly injects the active editor state into agent prompts. - **Model Selection**: Exposed as an ACP config option, so the in-session model dropdown works. - **Thinking Level**: Jcode reports the provider's reasoning efforts as an <code>effort</code> config option, so the thinking-level dropdown works with it. - **Queued messages**: Jcode rejects a second <code>session/prompt</code> while a turn runs ("already processing a prompt"), so a message you send mid-turn waits in the [[Queuing Messages]] toolbar queue until the turn ends. - **Session reload**: Jcode implements <code>session/load</code> and advertises <code>session/close</code>/<code>session/resume</code>, so [[Reloading a Session]] works for sessions Jcode has already persisted. - **Slash Commands**: Jcode advertises its slash-command set over the protocol, so its commands appear in the command palette with their descriptions. - **Token statistics**: Jcode sends <code>usage&#95;update</code> notifications and per-turn token figures, so context size and token counts are recorded; cost stays empty because Jcode reports no price. #### Limitations The harness chooser labels Jcode <b>Limited</b>; the items below are what that badge points to. See [[Onboarding]]. - **No plugin MCP tools**: Jcode validates the ACP <code>mcpServers</code> field but does not start those servers yet, so BeanBot does not hand it the plugin's internal MCP server and the <code>nb&#95;&#95;*</code> tools are unavailable. Configure MCP servers in Jcode's own configuration if you need them. - **No session list from Jcode**: Jcode does not implement <code>session/list</code>, so the session dropdown only shows sessions tracked locally by this BeanBot instance — sessions created in another Jcode client do not appear. - **No agent/mode selector**: Jcode exposes no mode request and no mode config option; only the model and reasoning-effort dropdowns are offered. Its approval and sandbox behavior is controlled by Jcode's own configuration. - **No IDE permission prompts**: Jcode's ACP adapter never sends <code>session/request&#95;permission</code>, so BeanBot's **Allow Once / Always Allow / Reject** panel does not appear for its edits and commands. Keep the project under version control and review changes with your VCS, or use Jcode's own approval settings. - **Queued messages**: Jcode rejects a prompt sent during a running turn instead of folding it in, so BeanBot holds the message until turn end (see [[Queuing Messages]]). Interleaved agents such as [[OpenCode]] send immediately instead. - **Model switching path**: BeanBot changes the model through Jcode's <code>model</code> config option and the thinking level through <code>effort</code>, not the dedicated model request. Both dropdowns show the options Jcode reports back, not a fixed list. > [[Post Install]] > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Onboarding]] > [[Queuing Messages]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]]
